environment.description: Same Celery worker code deployed in identical ECS Fargate configuration. The upstream API is fronted by an AWS API Gateway (HTTP API type) with a usage plan attached. The usage plan enforces a throttle of 5 requests per second per API key with a burst of 10, and a quota of 100 requests per day per authenticated client. When the rate limit is exceeded, API Gateway returns 429 Too Many Requests before the request reaches the Flask backend, meaning the Celery task is never dispatched. Additionally, the API Gateway has a request validator enabled on the /api/v1/user/sync endpoint that enforces a JSON schema requiring 'username' to match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,64}$ and 'department' to match ^[a-zA-Z\s]{0,128}$, rejecting non-conforming payloads with 400 before they reach the backend.

config.network: Private subnet, API Gateway (HTTP API) in front of Flask ALB
config.api_gateway_throttle: 5 req/s per key, burst 10, daily quota 100/client
config.api_gateway_request_validation: JSON schema on /api/v1/user/sync: username pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,64}$, department pattern ^[a-zA-Z\s]{0,128}$
config.ldap_service_account_permissions: Read access to entire dc=corp,dc=local tree
config.rate_limiting_response: 429 returned by API Gateway layer, Flask/Celery never invoked
config.input_validation_response: 400 returned by API Gateway for schema violations
